title: Telemetrics embeddings + rerank: batching, KV cache & latency SLO deep dive

transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2025-04-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Telemetrics, Head of ML), Priya Raman (Telemetrics, Platform), Samir Patel (Telemetrics, Data Scientist)
---
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, does 48 minutes still work?
[00:08] Jordan Lee: Yeah that's fine, thanks Alex.
[00:12] Maya Ortiz: Great, I'll share my screen in a sec, but main objective today is to go deep on embeddings + rerank perf and cost tradeoffs, especially around vector dims, batching, and the KV cache impacts.
[00:29] Priya Raman: Awesome. To set context, we have a ~20M document corpus, typical query QPS is 50 average peak 200, rerank stage ranks top 100 candidates and we need p95 < 200ms for rerank end-to-end ideally. Embedding endpoint target is p95 < 50ms.
[00:50] Alex Kim: Perfect. And what's your current embedding vector dimension?
[00:54] Samir Patel: Right now for experiments we use 768 dims from an off-the-shelf open model but it's expensive. We're evaluating 128 and 512 to see cost/accuracy tradeoffs.
[01:10] Maya Ortiz: Cool. High-level: lower dims reduce compute and memory, faster inference and smaller index cost, but can impact rerank recall. We recommend benchmarking 128/256/512. For throughput, batching strategy is key — large batches for embeddings improve GPU throughput but hurt latency.
[01:34] Jordan Lee: On batching — we were thinking of batching at the request level in the app to 64. Is that sensible?
[01:40] Maya Ortiz: 64 is a common start. On Dedicated you can sustain batch 64 with good GPU utilization; on hosted low-latency SLOs can be met with smaller batches or prefix KV cache for rerank. If you need p95 < 50ms for single-embedding queries, batching at 64 will likely push you above that unless you accept higher p95.
[02:02] Priya Raman: Can you say more about KV cache for rerank? We saw mention of "K-V cache" in your docs but not sure how it helps candidate rerank.
[02:10] Maya Ortiz: Sure — so KV cache stores key/value states for previous tokens during autoregressive generation. For rerank, we use prefix caching when re-scoring candidates that share history or partial contexts. Practically, if your rerank flow reuses encoder outputs or shared prefixes, caching can avoid re-compute which reduces latency by up to 30-60% depending on hit rates. Note: cache hit-rate depends on traffic patterns, prompt reuse.
[02:40] Samir Patel: Hmm, our rerank calls are independent per query but many queries share templates. So maybe 20-30% hit rate expected.
[02:50] Maya Ortiz: That will still help. Also batching at the step that uses GPU can be decoupled from network batching using Redwood's continuous batching layer — we can aggregate requests for a few milliseconds to build efficient kernels without adding big tail latency.
[03:05] Jordan Lee: You mentioned quantization. How does q4_0 compare to int8 or fp16 for embedding quality and latency?
[03:12] Maya Ortiz: q4_0 is a 4-bit quant technique that's very cost-effective. For many embedding models, q4_0 only marginally reduces nearest-neighbor accuracy vs fp16 while cutting memory by ~2-4x. int8 can be trickier, sometimes needs calibration; latency wise q4_0 and int8 both speed up inference significantly compared to fp32, but q4_0 often gives the best cost/throughput tradeoff on our runtime.
[03:40] Alex Kim: Worth noting, some customers see a small degradation on strict recall tasks — so validate with your test set.
[03:48] Priya Raman: For our rerank, recall at top 10 matters. We'll supply sample sets.
[03:56] Maya Ortiz: Perfect. For the bench we'll run: dims 128 vs 512, quant modes: fp16, q4_0; batch sizes: 1, 16, 64; measure p50/p95/p99, and per-1M-cost estimate.
[04:18] Jordan Lee: How do we think about index size & vector store cost? If we go 512 vs 128 dims that's 4x storage.
[04:24] Maya Ortiz: Yes, index size scales linearly with dim. And search latency can be affected by vector size too — bigger vectors increase memory bandwidth load. For cost projections we'll include storage + retrieval cost per million queries using a FAISS-like baseline.
[04:40] Samir Patel: Can you explain routing/fallbacks? In peak times we might spill to cheaper model variants.
[04:45] Alex Kim: Redwood supports smart routing policies — route by latency, cost, or region. For rerank you can have a cheaper fallback that produces reasonable scores if primary model is overloaded. That can be automatic if p95 spikes.
[04:58] Jordan Lee: On VPC/on-prem — our security team is strict. The private deployment needs to keep keys on-prem, with KMS integration and audit logs.
[05:07] Maya Ortiz: Understood. Our Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logging. There's a checklist we'll share; the on-prem package requires certain GPU drivers and kernel versions. We'll schedule a security deep dive with your infra team.
[05:26] Priya Raman: Any differences in batching/latency on-prem vs hosted?
[05:30] Maya Ortiz: The runtime is the same, but on-prem you control instance sizing; Dedicated and Private allow more aggressive batch sizing because you reserve capacity and can tune kernels. Hosted also benefits from autoscaling but for tight SLOs Dedicated/Private gives predictable p95.
[05:51] Samir Patel: For a pilot, what config would you recommend?
[05:55] Maya Ortiz: Start with 3 bench variants: A) 128 dim q4_0 batch 16; B) 512 dim q4_0 batch 16; C) 512 dim fp16 batch 8. Measure p95 rerank and embedding latency, plus recall delta vs your baseline. Also track cache hit-rate and end-to-end rerank time (search + embed + model rerank).
[06:20] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Any gotchas around tokenization or embedding model mismatches when you quantize?
[06:26] Maya Ortiz: Tokenization shouldn't change; quantization affects numeric representation post-embedding. But if your reranker uses cross-encoder re-ranking (full attention), quantization errors might affect fine-grained score differences. We log and surface those in Redwood Console's quality monitors.
[06:45] Alex Kim: Quick note on cost: we can provide a per-1M queries cost sheet factoring compute, storage, and network. We'll include Dedicated pricing and hosted tiers.
[06:57] Priya Raman: Great. Jordan: what's your target timeline?
[07:01] Jordan Lee: We want an internal pilot within 3 weeks, and a production decision in 2 months. So bench results next week are critical.
[07:10] Alex Kim: We'll prioritize that.
[07:12] [07:12] Maya Ortiz: I'll talk through some preliminary numbers — pulling up the bench template now (screen share).
[07:20] [07:20] Maya Ortiz: Example numbers: 128 dim q4_0 embed batch1 p95 ~30-45ms, batch16 p95 ~55-80ms; 512 dim q4_0 batch1 p95 ~45-70ms, batch16 ~80-140ms, fp16 slightly slower than q4_0 on memory heavy models for our runtime. These vary by GPU type and kernel.
[07:48] Samir Patel: Those look promising. For rerank end-to-end, do you have numbers that combine search latency?
[07:54] Maya Ortiz: If you use ANN search with index shard colocated, search for top100 typically adds 20-80ms depending on index size and vector dimension. So end-to-end p95 for rerank could be embedding+p95 + search + model rerank. We'll model that in the sheet.
[08:12] Jordan Lee: Can Redwood run benchmarks on our sample dataset or do you need us to anonymize?
[08:18] Alex Kim: We can run on a synthetic dataset that mirrors your characteristics, or if you can provide anonymized sample set that's preferred for accuracy. We'll never persist your raw data on hosted without agreement — for Private/Dedicated we can run in your VPC.
[08:34] Priya Raman: For Private, do you provide the control plane or do we host everything?
[08:38] Maya Ortiz: Private offers customer-managed network with Redwood control plane optionally hosted in your VPC; on-prem is fully customer-hosted. We'll outline both options in the security pack.
[08:52] Jordan Lee: Any performance differences in prefix caching between hosted and on-prem?
[08:56] Maya Ortiz: Mechanically same cache behavior. On-prem you can tune cache sizes and persistence. Hosted caches are optimized across shards but storage persistence and TTL are configurable.
[09:08] Samir Patel: About rollout: can we do canary where a fraction of traffic uses high-dim model for A/B?
[09:13] Alex Kim: Yes — Redwood rollouts support canary and percentage routing, with automatic fallback if SLOs are missed. We'll show you console config in follow-up.
[09:25] Jordan Lee: Let's talk about the cost model for Dedicated vs hosted for our QPS.
[09:30] Maya Ortiz: For 50 QPS sustained, Dedicated reserved pools are often more economical and give predictable latency. We have a cost model template — we'll fill it for your numbers in the shared spreadsheet.
[09:44] Alex Kim: Quick clarification — when you said peak 200 QPS, is that burst or sustained for 10s of minutes?
[09:50] Priya Raman: Typically bursty for a few minutes, not sustained.
[09:54] Maya Ortiz: Good to know; that influences autoscale and buffer capacity.
[10:00] Jordan Lee: Any constraints on GPUs for quantized models?
[10:05] Maya Ortiz: q4_0 benefits from GPUs with good tensor core support; our runtime picks kernels accordingly. On some older hardware q4_0 may fall back to slower paths, we'll note GPU recommendations.
[10:20] Samir Patel: For benchmarks, can you log embeddings L2 distances and recall metrics?
[10:25] Maya Ortiz: Yes, we'll provide per-query logs and summary metrics. We'll also include config used for FAISS/ANN.
[10:33] Jordan Lee: Great. On security, Priya will want SAML/SSO, RBAC and audit logs.
[10:40] Alex Kim: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning and RBAC, and detailed audit logs. For Private we can integrate with your IdP.
[10:49] Priya Raman: Perfect. One more thing — network egress costs for vector store access?
[10:55] Maya Ortiz: If index and runtime are in same region/VPC egress is minimal. We'll include network assumptions in the cost sheet.
[11:05] Jordan Lee: OK, timeline recap?
[11:08] Alex Kim: Redwood runs bench, Telemetrics provides data set, we reconvene in one week to review.
[11:14] [11:14] Maya Ortiz: I'll send the bench template and a recommended Dedicated config.
[11:20] Jordan Lee: Thanks — anything else?
[11:23] Samir Patel: One micro point — how do you measure cache hit-rate?
[11:27] Maya Ortiz: Console exposes hit-rate per route and TTLs. For the bench we'll report raw hits per candidate and effective latency delta.
[11:36] Alex Kim: Okay wrapping up. We'll capture action items and follow-ups. Thanks all.
[11:42] Jordan Lee: Thanks.
